text:
Google Unity launches no-code game creation platform Playground

Google and Unity have just dropped a new platform called Playground that promises to let anyone create games without needing any coding skills. So, what’s really different about this one? Why should it matter to you? And how does it stack up against the competition?

Playground is designed for those who dream of creating their own video games but lack the technical know-how or time to learn programming languages. The platform allows users to describe their game concepts through text prompts, and then uses advanced natural language processing (NLP) to generate fully playable games behind the scenes. This means you can tweak characters, rules, physics, and settings using simple commands—no coding required.
How Does Playground Work?

The process is straightforward: start by choosing a genre or starting from scratch if you have something unique in mind. For instance, imagine describing a dream-themed platformer where players climb through clouds in both normal and speedrun modes. With Playground, all it takes are a few text prompts to bring that vision to life. The platform handles everything else, including character animations and level design.

Let’s break down the steps:

1. Choose Your Genre: Select from popular genres like Trivia, Tower Defense, Racing, or start from scratch.
2. Describe Your Concept: Use simple text prompts to describe your game mechanics, characters, and settings.
3. Generate Your Game: The platform uses NLP to interpret your descriptions and generates a playable game.

For example, if you want to create a trivia game where players protect the temple of truth, you might input something like: "A fast-paced reaction and trivia game where players protect the temple of truth." Playground will then generate a fully functional game complete with mechanics and visuals based on your description.
What’s the Big Deal?

For hobbyists and casual gamers who have always wanted to create their own games but lacked the technical know-how, Playground is a significant step forward. It democratizes game development by lowering the barrier to entry significantly. No more slogging through coding tutorials or wrestling with complex software—just describe your idea, hit start, and watch it come to life.
Multiplayer Modes and Leaderboards

Playground supports multiplayer modes and leaderboards for various genres, adding another layer of interactivity to your creations. This means you can not only create games but also share them with others and compete in real-time. Whether you’re into trivia, tower defense, racing, or something entirely unique, the platform offers a wide range of options.

For instance, if you create a multiplayer trivia game, players from around the world can join your leaderboard and compete for top scores. This feature not only enhances user engagement but also provides a social aspect to game creation.
Unity Spark: The Next Big Thing

The most exciting part is Unity Spark, an upcoming feature that will add full 3D scenes and more complex game mechanics powered by Unity’s engine. A closed beta for this enhanced version is expected to launch soon, promising even greater possibilities for game creators.

Unity Spark will allow users to create intricate 3D environments and implement advanced gameplay features such as physics simulations, particle effects, and AI-driven characters. This upgrade will cater to more experienced developers looking to push the boundaries of what’s possible with Playground.
What Is Stored?

When you use Playground, your text prompts and the resulting games are stored on Google's servers. This includes any custom settings or rules you’ve defined through the platform’s interface. However, it doesn’t store personal information like your name or email address unless you choose to provide it voluntarily for support purposes.

For example, if you create a game called "Pitfalls," all the text prompts and generated content will be stored on Google's servers, but no personal data beyond what you explicitly share will be retained.
What Is Excluded?

Playground does not save user-generated content beyond what is necessary for generating and playing games. It excludes any sensitive data such as financial details or health records. Additionally, the platform does not retain any chat logs or messages exchanged during game creation unless explicitly requested by you for troubleshooting issues.

This ensures that your personal information remains private while still allowing you to leverage the full capabilities of Playground’s creative tools.
User Controls

Users have control over their creations through a variety of settings within the Playground interface. You can adjust gameplay mechanics, character designs, and even add custom elements like sound effects or background music. However, these controls are limited to what’s provided in the platform's menu options—no direct coding access here.

For example, if you want to change the background color of your game, you simply select from a predefined list of colors rather than writing CSS code. This makes it easy for anyone to customize their games without needing programming knowledge.
Availability

Playground is currently only available in the United States to users aged 18 and older. If you’re outside the US, you can still access it via a Virtual Private Network (VPN). The limits of what you can generate depend on your Google AI subscription level, but exact pricing details haven’t been released yet.

This means that while Playground is accessible globally through workarounds like VPNs, its official rollout and full feature set are currently limited to specific regions and age groups. 
What This Does Not Prove

While Playground offers an incredible starting point for creativity, it’s important to note that the AI-generated code might not be as polished or efficient as what a professional developer would create. There are no guarantees that every game concept will translate perfectly into playable form. Plus, the platform is currently limited to certain regions and age groups.

For example, while Playground can generate a basic trivia game with ease, it may struggle with more complex mechanics like real-time multiplayer interactions or advanced physics simulations. Additionally, users outside the US might face technical challenges when using VPNs to access the platform.
Practical Takeaway

So give it a shot if you’re up for it—Playground is live now, even if it’s not officially available to everyone yet. Are you ready to turn your game ideas into reality?

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

News

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
July 13, 1978. Ford fired the man who built the Mustang. Exactly five years later, he got his revenge.

Iacocca had given Ford 32 years. He was the father of the Mustang and the president of the company. Ford made close to $2 billion that year.

On July 13, 1978, Henry Ford II fired him anyway. Asked why, Ford reportedly said: sometimes you just don't like somebody.

Iacocca later called it a lonely summer. Big companies outside cars offered him the top job. He wanted to stay in cars, and the only real opening was Chrysler. It was close to bankruptcy.

He cut his own salary to $1 a year. He laid off tens of thousands of workers, and he says he never forgot their faces. He went to Washington and won federal loan guarantees, and Chrysler borrowed $1.2 billion. Then he went on TV himself: if you can find a better car, buy it.

On July 13, 1983, exactly five years after Ford fired him, he stood at the National Press Club in Washington. Chrysler would pay off the last $800 million. Seven years early.

He opened by saying he was fired five years ago that day and hated being reminded of it. Then came his line: we at Chrysler borrow money the old-fashioned way. We pay it back.

Henry Ford II fired a man he did not like. He ended up handing a rival the one executive who knew how to beat him.

Be honest. Was firing him Henry Ford II's right call, or the biggest mistake Ford ever made?

It seems President @DonaldJTrump has done something unthinkable, again.

In an interview with Fox News, ambassador (to China) @DavidPerdueGA said “President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world,’” adding “He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”

For context, US law strictly prohibits arms sales to China. Butt Trump's offer to #China would not just defy law, but also logic.

The offer basically translates into Trump wanting to sell weapons to Iran's most powerful ally at the same time as he uses them against #Iran!

It is a claim that President Trump has denied but if anyone thinks about it carefully, diplomats do not make unfounded statements, ever.

It is apparent President Trump mentioned this to President Xi but decided to roll back on his words; perhaps because he was later educated by officials trying to save face about the President making promises to the US’ adversaries.

That too, not just any adversary, but China - a country that Washington officially identifies as its primary strategic and economic competitor.

Let's delve a little deeper into the implications of such a statement.

The US still has considerable edge over its adversaries by means of commanding an arsenal of high-tech sophisticated weapons, which is the basis of national security.

That advantage acts as a deterrent for the country’s adversaries to engage militarily. And here the President of the country has offered to sell, quite literally, the national security away to its biggest rivals.

Allies of #America would be dumbfounded that their strongest defence partner in mutual security engagements, has decided to effectively sell itself out.

Former and current officials were scrambling to mitigate the unforeseen damage that the President's loose remarks may have caused. The @WhiteHouse and the State Department both clarified that the U.S. government has no plans to sell weapons to China.

So thankfully, Americans do not need to worry about the President's gaffe for now... until his next gaffe (which may just be around the corner).

The White House and the State Department's remarks may have woken Trump up this time, to eat his words. 

But how long will this circus of a Presidency go on?

Today, we can go to bed today in peace thanking the foresight of some of our predecessors who put the law into place to bridle whimsical tyrants like Trump, but what about tomorrow?!

text:
JAPÃO E MÉXICO: A NOVA GEOGRAFIA DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL PASSA PELA AMÉRICA LATINA

O Japão deixou de apenas observar a reorganização industrial da América do Norte.

Agora, procura participar de sua arquitetura.
México e Japão concordaram em realizar, ainda no atual ano fiscal japonês, a primeira reunião do Diálogo Econômico de Alto Nível Japão–México.

O mecanismo deverá abranger segurança econômica, resiliência das cadeias produtivas, energia, ciência, tecnologia e infraestrutura. Os dois países também decidiram criar uma força-tarefa bilateral em nível de diretores-gerais, destinada a sustentar a relação no médio e no longo prazo.

Pode parecer apenas mais um dispositivo diplomático.

Não é.

O Japão está construindo uma presença institucional dentro de uma economia diretamente integrada aos Estados Unidos — e que se tornou, silenciosamente, uma peça importante da infraestrutura mundial de inteligência artificial.

O México já não exporta apenas automóveis

Em 2026, o México passou a fornecer aproximadamente 40% dos servidores importados pelos Estados Unidos para centros de dados de inteligência artificial.

Entre janeiro e maio, as vendas mexicanas de servidores empresariais aos Estados Unidos alcançaram US$ 46,9 bilhões. Esses equipamentos ultrapassaram os automóveis e se tornaram o principal produto mexicano destinado ao mercado norte-americano.
Essa transformação foi impulsionada sobretudo por fabricantes taiwaneses que instalaram ou ampliaram unidades de produção no México.

O país passou, assim, a ocupar uma posição singular:

recebe tecnologia e capital asiáticos;

monta equipamentos essenciais à inteligência artificial;

utiliza as vantagens comerciais do T-MEC;
abastece o mercado e os centros de dados dos Estados Unidos.
É dentro dessa estrutura que o Japão agora procura ampliar sua presença.
O Japão não chega como potência secundária

A diplomacia japonesa opera de maneira diferente da norte-americana e da chinesa.

Washington dispõe do peso de seu mercado, de tarifas, sanções e exigências de segurança. Pequim oferece escala financeira, infraestrutura e contratos de longo prazo.
O Japão tende a agir por outro caminho: investimento industrial, tecnologia, cooperação energética, formação de cadeias produtivas e mecanismos institucionais permanentes.

Não se trata de neutralidade.

Tóquio permanece integrado à arquitetura estratégica dos Estados Unidos. Mas pode contribuir para reorganizar cadeias norte-americanas sem reproduzir diretamente a coerção tarifária de Washington.

A aproximação com o México conecta três forças:

tecnologia e capital japoneses;

capacidade industrial mexicana;

demanda norte-americana por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.
Essa triangulação pode transformar o México em algo maior do que uma plataforma de nearshoring.
O país pode tornar-se um ponto de articulação entre empresas japonesas, fabricantes asiáticos e o sistema tecnológico dos Estados Unidos.

A China está presente mesmo quando não participa da reunião

Nenhum dos comunicados oficiais anunciou restrições contra empresas chinesas.

Mas a China constitui o pano de fundo estratégico.
A revisão das cadeias produtivas, as discussões sobre segurança econômica e a possível alteração das regras de origem do T-MEC podem aumentar o controle sobre componentes, propriedade empresarial e procedência tecnológica.

Hoje, um servidor montado no México pode receber tratamento comercial favorável mesmo quando diversos componentes vêm da Ásia — inclusive da China.

Essa situação dificilmente permanecerá fora da disputa estratégica.

Se Estados Unidos, Japão e México avançarem na construção de cadeias consideradas confiáveis, Pequim poderá perder espaço em setores tecnológicos sensíveis.

Mas o México também enfrentará um risco: tornar-se indispensável industrialmente sem conquistar autonomia tecnológica.

Montar servidores não equivale a controlar os semicondutores, os sistemas, o financiamento ou as decisões que organizam a cadeia.

O México ganha poder — mas ainda não autonomia

O novo diálogo amplia as possibilidades mexicanas.

O país poderá atrair investimentos japoneses, diversificar parceiros e reduzir sua dependência de uma relação exclusivamente bilateral com Washington.
Ao mesmo tempo, sua produção continua profundamente vinculada ao mercado norte-americano e dependente de componentes, empresas e tecnologias estrangeiras.

Há uma oportunidade e uma armadilha.

A oportunidade consiste em transformar a montagem de equipamentos em política industrial: criar fornecedores locais, formar engenheiros, incorporar tecnologia e aumentar o valor produzido dentro do país.

A armadilha consiste em permanecer como território de passagem — estratégico para todos, mas soberano sobre poucas decisões.

Uma mudança institucional antes da mudança material

O acordo entre Japão e México ainda não representa uma alteração financeira de grande escala.

Não foram divulgados valores de investimentos, fábricas específicas, projetos de inteligência artificial ou restrições formais a fornecedores chineses.
A mudança, neste momento, é institucional e direcional.

Mas instituições criam continuidade. Organizam interesses, aproximam empresas e transformam visitas diplomáticas em processos decisórios permanentes.

O Japão não está simplesmente retornando à América Latina.

Está procurando uma entrada própria na reorganização tecnológica da América do Norte.

E o México começa a descobrir que sua posição geográfica pode valer tanto quanto seus produtos.

A questão será saber se conseguirá converter essa posição em capacidade de decisão.

Fontes

Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Japão — reunião dos chanceleres de Japão e México

JAPAN AND MEXICO: THE NEW GEOGRAPHY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RUNS THROUGH LATIN AMERICA

Japan is no longer merely observing the industrial reorganization of North America.

It is now seeking a place within its architecture.
Mexico and Japan have agreed to hold the first meeting of the Japan–Mexico High-Level Economic Dialogue during the current Japanese fiscal year.

The mechanism is expected to address economic security, supply-chain resilience, energy, science, technology, and infrastructure. The two countries will also establish a director-general-level bilateral task force intended to strengthen the relationship over the medium and long term.

This may appear to be just another diplomatic mechanism.

It is not.

Japan is building an institutional presence inside an economy directly integrated with the United States — one that has quietly become an important component of the global artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

Mexico no longer exports only automobiles

In 2026, Mexico began supplying approximately 40% of the computer servers imported by the United States for artificial-intelligence data centers.

Between January and May, Mexican sales of enterprise servers to the United States reached $46.9 billion. These products overtook automobiles to become Mexico’s leading export to the U.S. market.
The transformation has been driven primarily by Taiwanese manufacturers expanding production in Mexico.

The country now occupies a distinctive position:

it receives Asian capital and technology;

assembles equipment essential to artificial intelligence;

benefits from USMCA trade arrangements;
supplies the U.S. market and its data centers.
It is within this structure that Japan is seeking to expand its presence.
Japan is not arriving as a secondary power

Japanese diplomacy operates differently from both the United States and China.

Washington commands the weight of its market, tariffs, sanctions, and security requirements. Beijing offers financial scale, infrastructure, and long-term contracts.
Japan tends to pursue another route: industrial investment, technology, energy cooperation, supply-chain development, and permanent institutional mechanisms.

This is not neutrality.

Tokyo remains integrated into the U.S.-led strategic architecture. But it can help reorganize North American supply chains without directly reproducing Washington’s tariff coercion.

The rapprochement with Mexico connects three forces:

Japanese capital and technology;

Mexican industrial capacity;

U.S. demand for artificial-intelligence infrastructure.
This triangulation could turn Mexico into more than a nearshoring platform.
It may become a point of connection between Japanese companies, Asian manufacturers, and the U.S. technology system.

China is present even when it is not in the room

None of the official statements announced restrictions against Chinese companies.

Yet China remains the strategic background.
Supply-chain reviews, economic-security discussions, and possible changes to USMCA rules of origin may increase scrutiny of components, corporate ownership, and technological provenance.

Today, a server assembled in Mexico may receive preferential treatment even when many of its components originate in Asia — including China.

That reality is unlikely to remain outside the strategic dispute.

If the United States, Japan, and Mexico move toward building trusted supply chains, Beijing may lose ground in sensitive technological sectors.

But Mexico also faces a risk: becoming industrially indispensable without acquiring technological autonomy.

Assembling servers is not the same as controlling semiconductors, systems, financing, or the decisions that organize the supply chain.

Mexico gains leverage — but not yet autonomy

The new dialogue expands Mexico’s options.

The country may attract Japanese investment, diversify its partnerships, and reduce its dependence on an exclusively bilateral relationship with Washington.
At the same time, its production remains deeply tied to the U.S. market and dependent on foreign components, companies, and technologies.

There is an opportunity and a trap.

The opportunity is to transform equipment assembly into industrial policy: develop domestic suppliers, train engineers, absorb technology, and increase the value produced inside Mexico.

The trap is to remain a transit territory — strategically important to everyone, yet sovereign over few decisions.

An institutional change before a material one

The Japan–Mexico agreement does not yet represent a large-scale financial shift.

No specific investment figures, factories, artificial-intelligence projects, or formal restrictions on Chinese suppliers have been announced.
For now, the change is institutional and directional.

But institutions create continuity. They organize interests, connect companies, and transform diplomatic visits into permanent decision-making processes.

Japan is not simply returning to Latin America.

It is seeking its own entry into the technological reorganization of North America.

Mexico, meanwhile, is beginning to discover that its geographic position may be as valuable as the goods it produces.

The question is whether it can convert that position into decision-making power.

Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Japan–Mexico foreign ministers’ meeting

text:
Steve Eisman @realsteveeisman, of Big Short fame, made the bear case for online travel on the New Money podcast this week. $BKNG $EXPE

He tells his agent to book a flight to Miami and the best hotel, and the agent goes through every travel site, finds the best price, and books it. 

As Eisman put it: 

“You’re not their customer anymore. Your AI agent is the customer.” 

He then asks the obvious follow-up: 

What exactly is Booking’s switching moat if you never visit the website again?

It’s worth being precise about which moat he’s questioning. It’s a habit moat. You open the app, you compare, you book, and after a few years the opening becomes a reflex. An agent that queries every site and books the cheapest option has no reflexes and no favorite apps. If the customer relationship moves from the site to the agent, the advertising money that paid for that traffic moves with it. 

Eisman contrasts this with software deeply embedded in the enterprise. A company like ServiceNow, or one of Constellation Software’s vertical market businesses, sits inside the daily operations of a firm, with the data, the trained staff, and the switching costs already in place. An agent can shop for a flight. Ripping out the system a company runs on is a different matter.

I think that distinction is directionally correct, and it explains why travel sits at the top of nearly every list of potential victims. 

It’s also, however, where I think the debate has become lazy and needs a little more nuance.

Let me steelman the bear case first, because it’s genuinely unsettling. It’s easy to picture an agent that checks every online travel agency and every hotel’s own website, then comes back with the three best options. 

In that world, Booking and Expedia lose a slice of their bookings to direct channels wherever the hotel offers a better price. 

That’s what makes agentic AI such a scary proposition for an intermediary: it turns every consumer into a ruthless shopper, a real-world homo oeconomicus, who is purely rational in his decision-making and also happens to be omniscient. 

Two decades of brand building, app downloads and loyalty perks count for little if your customer is a piece of software that only cares about the final price, or the best bang for the buck.

The problem with this scenario is that it describes what can theoretically be built and skips the question of how anyone would build it today – the first question we raised in the segment above. 

Booking-com started in 1996 as a small Dutch startup, and the bulk of what it built over the following three decades happened on the ground. It set up local offices across Europe and later Asia and Latin America, with account managers who walked into independent hotels, family-run B&Bs and guesthouses and signed them up one by one. The pitch was simple and unusually generous for its time: no upfront fee and no marketing budget, only a commission once a guest had actually stayed. That model fit Europe's fragmented hotel market in particular, where most rooms belong to independent owners rather than large chains, and every one of those owners had to be onboarded, have their photos and room types loaded, connected to rate and availability feeds, and supported in their own language when something went wrong. Layer after layer of that work compounded into a supply base that, as of December 2025, stood at 32 million listings across 4.4 million properties, along with decades of verified reviews, payment infrastructure and customer service that guests and hotels have come to trust. Rebuilding that from scratch would be close to impossible for a new entrant, because supply alone does not make a hotel owner sign up. They join for the demand Booking brings, and a challenger without bookings to offer is asking a busy owner to do onboarding work for nothing. 

An agent has no live inventory link to the vast majority of hotels. To find out whether a room is available at a given price, it has to go through the booking flow on each website, step by step, almost as if it were going to book. The answer can be different an hour later, because hotel pricing is dynamic and changes constantly. The best OTA rates are often only visible to logged-in members – Booking’s Genius discounts being the obvious example – so an agent that scrapes the public page doesn’t even see the cheapest price. 

And contrary to popular belief, going direct often isn’t cheaper. Hotels frequently give OTAs discounted rates for members, which means the Booking price can be lower than the one on the hotel’s own website. 

Repeating all of that for every property, for every query, from every user, is extraordinarily compute-intensive and slow.

Another interesting question for agentic AI is whether that replication is even necessary. An agent sitting between the traveller and the booking doesn’t need to rebuild the network if it can rent it through Booking, Expedia or the chains’ own direct APIs and channel managers, which have made the plumbing far more standardized than it was twenty years ago. 

I find a library a helpful analogy. Imagine you’re looking for a book, and there’s a librarian who knows where every book is and what each one is about. You refuse to talk to her. Instead, you pick up every book in the library, read each one, and only then decide which one you wanted. 

Then it gets even crazier, because you repeat the whole exercise every time you need a book. That’s roughly what an agent does when it bypasses the OTAs. Booking has spent more than 25 years building the infrastructure that knows where every room is, what it costs right now, and what other guests thought of it. An agent can, in theory, rebuild that index from scratch on every request. Whether that makes sense as a product, given the compute bill and the waiting time, is another question.

<RIGGED> is recruiting on World of Warcraft: Forever - EU PVP / Horde

RIGGED is a tight-knit guild for VTubers and friends looking to take on everything WoW: Forever has to offer. Levelling, dungeons, world PvP, raids or fun events, there's something for everyone, and it might just be your Forever home.

DM or reply if interested!

== Where we're at ==
WoW: Forever is in beta until 21 October, with the full launch on Thursday, 5 November 2026 at Midnight (CET). A few of us are already playing the beta, but most will log in for the first time during launch night, and a lot of us are completely new to WoW. New players are very welcome!

== What we're doing ==
We're a casual guild in the sense that fun, community and team bonding come first. We are going to be doing raids and world PvP, but raids won't have a set roster. Signups are first come, first served, with a few spots reserved for core roles such as main tanks, healers and class leaders. For bigger 40-mans like Onyxia, we may team up with another guild.

We'll also host fun events like team vs team, hide and seek, and transmog competitions (yes, transmog exists in Forever. I'll mostly play without it, but it is undeniably fun).

== A bit about me ==
Hi, I'm Samu! I am an arctic fox VTuber!
My channel is Samurime on Twitch and YouTube. My Oshi is @Vedal987 and my rolemodel is @cerberVT

My main in Classic has always been Warrior, and that's the plan this time too (although Paladin is looking very tempting). I'll also be levelling some alts.

I've played WoW since around 2012, including the 2019 Vanilla Classic release, plus a bit of TBC Classic, SoD, Hardcore and Classic Anniversary. I cleared everything through AQ40 in both 2019 and Anniversary. In retail I've had Cutting Edge across multiple tiers, usually on Disc Priest.

I'm looking forward to our sharing our adventures!

KEY MESSAGES REGARDING ISAIAS IN SOUTHERN MIDDLE TENNESSEE: As we quickly approach "go time" for Isaias, I'm going to transition our morning updates to a KEY MESSAGES format. This should help keep the information clear, concise, and easy to follow without getting caught up in all the smaller details we've already discussed over the past several days.

TRACK & TIMING: Isaias is expected to make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast, most likely somewhere near the Mississippi, Alabama, or western Florida coastal region, late Friday night into early Saturday morning as a hurricane. From there, the system will move inland VERY quickly (and I mean VERY quickly), weakening as it does so. The center of circulation could be approaching the Tennessee state line roughly 12 hours after landfall. For Southern Middle Tennessee, the primary window for impacts currently looks to be from around sunrise Saturday through early Sunday morning, with the most impactful rainfall and strongest wind gusts potentially developing Saturday morning and continuing through the afternoon. Additional periods of moderate to heavy rainfall may continue Saturday evening and overnight, even as the strongest winds begin to subside. Scattered showers will also be possible outside this window, but the primary concern remains Saturday.

EXPECTED RAINFALL: Most of Southern Middle Tennessee is expected to receive between 1 and 2 inches of rainfall, although localized totals approaching 3 inches cannot be ruled out, especially where heavier rain bands develop. We will likely begin with a period of light to moderate, steady rainfall around or before sunrise Saturday, transitioning to heavier, more organized rain bands throughout the morning and afternoon as the circulation approaches. Additional rainfall could continue into Saturday night before gradually tapering off Sunday. By the time Isaias reaches our area, it is expected to have weakened substantially, potentially to a tropical depression. While some localized flooding issues cannot be ruled out, widespread significant flooding is not currently anticipated.

EXPECTED WIND GUSTS: Winds will likely become increasingly gusty Saturday morning, with the strongest gusts currently favored from late Saturday morning through the afternoon hours as the circulation approaches and moves through the region. At this point, gusts between 30 and 45 MPH appear possible, with a few isolated gusts approaching or exceeding 50 MPH not entirely out of the question. I do NOT currently expect widespread gusts of 50+ MPH. However, interactions between the transitioning tropical circulation and an approaching upper-level trough could help enhance winds in some locations. Even with gusts in the 30–45 MPH range, a few downed tree limbs and isolated power outages would be possible, particularly where the ground becomes saturated. Winds should gradually diminish Saturday evening and overnight as the system continues moving north.

A QUICK-HITTING SYSTEM: One important thing to understand is that Isaias will NOT be hanging around for several days. This is expected to be a relatively fast-moving system, with the most significant wind impacts concentrated during the daylight hours Saturday. Widespread rainfall will likely begin around sunrise Saturday, with several hours of heavier rainfall possible through the afternoon and evening. Additional rain bands could linger into the overnight hours before becoming more scattered Sunday morning. Some scattered showers could continue through Sunday afternoon or evening, but conditions should improve considerably by Sunday night, with quieter weather returning Monday. Again, Saturday will be the primary day to watch, although the exact timing of the heaviest rainfall will depend on the track and forward speed of Isaias.

ONE IMPORTANT NOTE ABOUT OUTDOOR EVENTS: I know there are a TON of outdoor events, fall festivals, sporting events, and other activities planned across Southern Middle Tennessee this weekend. I completely understand why everyone wants to know exactly what to expect for their specific event. Unfortunately, it is extremely difficult for me to individually answer every single question, although I certainly try to respond to as many as possible! The good news is that almost every answer can be found somewhere in my recent social media updates or blog posts. I strongly encourage you to read through those updates, especially as we get closer to Saturday. With the current timing, Saturday morning and afternoon activities appear to face the greatest risk of disruptive weather, although rain could continue into Saturday evening and overnight.

THE BOTTOM LINE: We're increasingly confident that Isaias will bring a period of soaking rainfall and gusty winds to Southern Middle Tennessee this weekend, particularly on Saturday. However, we're NOT expecting anywhere near hurricane conditions here at home. Our main window for impacts runs from sunrise Saturday through early Sunday morning, with the strongest wind gusts most likely Saturday morning and afternoon. The system will weaken rapidly as it moves inland, and impacts should come and go relatively quickly. As always, adjustments to the track, timing, rainfall totals, and wind gusts remain possible, so continue checking back for the latest updates!

BREAKING: Pakistan has directly joined the Saudi-led military campaign against Yemen’s Houthis, with Pakistani Air Force fighter jets now reportedly conducting air strikes against Houthi targets, according to a senior Pakistani military official who spoke anonymously to The New York Times.

Around 8,000 Pakistani troops are already deployed in Saudi Arabia, including Air Force and Army air-defense personnel. Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered huge amounts of money to the Pakistani leadership.

Oil is also climbing as the fighting spreads across the region, with Brent crude reaching above $102 a barrel and WTI near $92.

text:
🇮🇳 A Proud and Inspiring Air Force Day at Air Force Station Hindon.

Shri Sunil Kumar Nagdawne, CMD, Pawan Hans Limited, visited Air Force Station Hindon on the occasion of Air Force Day and had the privilege of witnessing the spectacular Air Force Day Parade. The occasion was a fitting tribute to the courage, discipline, professionalism and unwavering commitment of the Indian Air Force and its brave air warriors, who continue to safeguard the nation with distinction and dedication.

The parade and ceremonial proceedings offered an inspiring glimpse into the remarkable capabilities, precision and operational excellence of the Indian Air Force, while reflecting the dedication of the men and women who remain steadfast in their service to the nation and in safeguarding India’s skies.

During the visit, Shri Sunil Kumar Nagdawne had the honor of meeting Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, PVSM, AVSM, Chief of the Air Staff, and conveyed his warm greetings and best wishes to him and the entire Indian Air Force fraternity on this proud occasion.

The Indian Air Force stands as a symbol of courage, professionalism, technological excellence and unwavering commitment to the nation. Its distinguished legacy of service and sacrifice continues to inspire generations and remains a source of immense pride for the nation.

Pawan Hans Limited extends its heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all serving personnel of the Indian Air Force, veterans and their families on Air Force Day.

Saluting the valor, dedication and indomitable spirit of our air warriors who continue to serve the nation with distinction. @Pib_MoCA @MoCA_GoI @Sunil_Nagdawne @IAFIndia 

🇮🇳 Jai Hind!
